{{Year in Russia|2000}}
The following lists events that happened during '''[[2000]] in [[Russia]]'''.

*[[Prime Minister of the Russian Federation|Prime Minister]]: [[Vladimir Putin]] (until May 7), [[Mikhail Kasyanov]] (from May 7)

==Events==
===February===
*February 4 — [[Second Chechen War]]: [[Bombing of Katyr-Yurt]]. 
*February 5 — Second Chechen War: [[Novye Aldi massacre]]. 
*February 6 — Second Chechen War: [[Battle of Grozny (1999–2000)|Battle of Grozny]], Chechen capital [[Grozny]] falls to Russian troops.<ref name="Cassell's Chronology">{{cite book|last=Williams|first=Hywel|title=Cassell's Chronology of World History|url=https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/649|url-access=registration|publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson|year=2005|isbn=0-304-35730-8|pages=[https://archive.org/details/cassellschronolo0000will/page/649 649–650]}}</ref>
*February 29–March 1 — Second Chechen War: [[Battle of Hill 776]].

===March===
*March — Second Chechen War: [[Komsomolskoye massacre]]. 
*March 1 — Second Chechen War: [[Grozny OMON fratricide incident]]. 
*March 4–25 — Second Chechen War: [[Battle of Komsomolskoye]].
*March 26 — [[2000 Russian presidential election|Presidential elections]]: [[Vladimir Putin]] is elected president.<ref name="Metro">{{cite news|title=[[Metro (Associated Metro Limited)|Metro]]|last=McGuinness|first=Ross|date=March 16, 2009|pages=30}}</ref>
*March 29 — Second Chechen War: [[Zhani-Vedeno ambush]].

===May===
*May 24 — The Russian Government threatens to bomb the [[Taliban]] in [[Afghanistan]] due to their support for Chechen rebels.<ref name="Cassell's Chronology"/>

===July===
*July 2–3 — Second Chechen War: [[Chechen suicide attacks]] kill 43 Russian soldiers.<ref name="Cassell's Chronology"/>

===August===
*August 12 — The [[Russian submarine K-141 Kursk|Russian submarine K-141 ''Kursk'']] sinks in the [[Barents Sea]], resulting in the [[Kursk submarine disaster|deaths]] of all 118 men on board.<ref name="Cassell's Chronology"/>
*August 14 — [[Tsar Nicholas II]] and several members of his family are canonized by the synod of the [[Russian Orthodox Church]].
*August 28 — Moscow's [[Ostankino Tower]] set ablaze by fire caused by a short circuit.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2000/WORLD/europe/08/27/moscow.fire/index.html |title = CNN.com - Fire rages in Moscow's giant TV tower - August 27, 2000  |website=www.cnn.com |access-date=11 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001002030519/http://www.cnn.com/2000/WORLD/europe/08/27/moscow.fire/index.html |archive-date=2 October 2000 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===September===
*September 15–October 1 — [[Russia at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Russia]] competes at the [[2000 Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics]] in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]], winning 32 gold, 28 silver and 29 bronze medals.

===December===
*December 25 — Russia changes their [[National anthem of Russia|national anthem]] back to the old [[Soviet Union]] [[State Anthem of the Soviet Union|anthem]], with newer lyrics.
